[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guide defines the **UI Contract** — the deterministic, declarative interface specification that makes a Presentation-layer feature buildable and dispatchable in the architecture pipeline (GUID-GOV-PROC-016). It is the Presentation-layer counterpart to the Implementation Design Document (IDD): a self-contained artifact, referenced from the pipeline rather than inlined.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Closes the UI gap** — the pipeline is spec-driven, and UI requirements (layout, interaction, state, data binding, accessibility) do not decompose into Gherkin the way backend logic does. Without a dedicated artifact, UI surfaces get *designed* (in conceptual and logical architecture) but never become *buildable requirements*, so a Presentation layer can reach "complete" with no implemented UI.
- **Deterministic and verifiable** — the contract is schema-validated JSON whose accessibility values are drawn from WAI-ARIA, so it can be checked by automated gates (axe-core, jest-axe, `@axe-core/playwright`) the way Gherkin is checked for backend logic.
- **Familiar to practitioners** — each section delegates to the de-facto industry standard for its concern, so UI/UX designers and front-end engineers recognize the parts they own.
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

- **UI/UX designers** — author the design tokens and accessibility patterns the contract carries
- **Solution and application architects** — own the framework/component-library decisions the contract references
- **Front-end engineers and AI coding agents** — consume the contract as the binding build specification
page_texts.7:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#scope-and-applicability]

### Scope and Applicability

This guide applies to any project in the architecture pipeline that has a **Presentation layer** (a `Layer = Presentation` component in the logical architecture, or a capability marked `UI Surface = Yes` in the conceptual architecture). Projects with no UI surface do not produce UI Contracts.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#where-the-ui-contract-sits-in-the-pipeline]

### Where the UI Contract sits in the pipeline

The UI Contract is produced and consumed across the existing pipeline stages — it does not add a new stage:

```text
Stage 6  Conceptual    →  capability marked  UI Surface = Yes        (declarative seed)
Stage 7  Functional    →  .feature gains @UI tag + @FR-*-UI- scenarios (additive)
Stage 8  Logical        →  /ui-designer writes TS-UI-* tech-specs       (tactical design)
         UI Contract     →  UIC-*.json authored from that analysis       (this artifact)
Stage 10 Export         →  surfaced into agent tasks; agent:ui dispatch
Final    Health check   →  Presentation reconciliation gate
```
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#relationship-to-the-idd]

### Relationship to the IDD

The UI Contract and the IDD are siblings. They share the **delivery channel** — both are surfaced into agent tasks through the issue's *Implementation Design Reference* section — but differ in two ways:

| Aspect | IDD | UI Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Format | Markdown design analysis | Schema-validated JSON |
| Optionality | Optional, forward-looking | **Mandatory** when the feature carries `@UI` |
| Gate | None | Must reach `approved` before the UI implementation issue is dispatched |
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#composite-standard-design]

### Composite-standard design

There is no single industry JSON standard that fully specifies a UI. The UI Contract is therefore a **composite**: a JSON Schema envelope, with each section delegating to the de-facto standard for its concern.

| Section | Industry standard | Recognized by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `designTokens` | **W3C Design Tokens (DTCG)** — `design-tokens.json` | Designers (Figma Tokens Studio), Style Dictionary |
| `screens[].forms` | **JSON Forms / RJSF UI Schema** over **JSON Schema** | Front-end engineers |
| `screens[].states` | **Storybook Component Story Format (CSF)** | Front-end engineers |
| `accessibility` | **WAI-ARIA + ARIA APG** | Accessibility & UX practitioners |
| `screens[]` (layout, data binding) | Modeled explicitly (no single JSON standard) | — |

ARIA is a vocabulary, not a JSON format — so the `accessibility` section is JSON whose *values* are drawn from ARIA roles/states and APG pattern names, keeping it both familiar and deterministically testable.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#required-structure]

### Required structure

A UI Contract instance MUST contain, at minimum:

1. **Identity** — `contractId` (`UIC-<CONCERN-ABBR>-<NNN>`), `feature` (path to the `@UI` `.feature` file), `boundedContext`, `component` (the `Layer = Presentation` logical component it realizes), `status`, `kind` (`screen` default, or `foundation`), a top-level **`version`** (SemVer), and — for a screen contract — `dependsOn` listing its app foundation contract (see "The app-foundation contract" below). **The `version` field is born at `1.0.0` when `/eap-decom-ui-contract-create` authors the contract** (not back-stamped later) and is the UI Contract's drift-detection marker — the same role `info.version` plays for OpenAPI/AsyncAPI seams. `--modify` bumps it (SemVer per TS-API-VER-02); `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` reads it into the `Built-From` stamp and `/eap-sdd-health-check --drift` reads it to detect a shipped screen that lags a changed contract (by version, not raw byte diff — a same-version reformat is not drift).
2. **`screens[]`** — one per view, each with layout `regions`, `dataBindings`, optional `forms`, `states` (the canonical loading/empty/populated/error set), `navigation`, and `responsive` behavior.
3. **`accessibility`** — REQUIRED: a `conformanceTarget` (WCAG level) and the ARIA APG `patterns[]` the screens implement, with required roles, keyboard interactions, and live regions.
4. **`dataBindings[]` with dependency tier and a shared contract reference** — each binding records its `source` (human-readable summary), a **`contractRef`** (REQUIRED — a `$ref` to a shared endpoint contract), `producingService`, and `dependencyTier` (T1/T2/T3). This array is the **authoritative source of the UI→backend prerequisite** that export uses to sequence the UI issue.
   - **`contractRef` — the consumer-driven-contract link.** Every cross-agent binding MUST `$ref` a **`sync-api` Seam Contract operation** authored at design time — a JSON-Pointer into the backing service's **OpenAPI 3.1** document (`docs/design/seam-contracts/sync-api/<service>/openapi.json#/paths/<escaped-path>/<method>`, produced in logical architecture Phase 4.5 — see the integration-architecture phase). The UI Contract is the *consumer* declaration for a **UI↔API seam**; the OpenAPI operation is the shared artifact both the UI/BFF consumer and the backend API producer bind to. (The seam contract family is authored in native standards per class — OpenAPI for `sync-api`, AsyncAPI for `event`, OPA/Rego for `cross-cutting` — see GUID-GOV-PROC-015; the UI Contract only ever references the `sync-api` class.) This is the single artifact the consumer binds to and the producer is *generated from and verified against*, so the UI/BFF agent and the backend API agent build to one schema instead of drifting. A bare DTO name or an inline schema is **not** valid for a cross-agent binding. If the endpoint has no OpenAPI operation yet, author it first; do not invent a shape in the UI Contract. Export **halts** on a binding whose `contractRef` does not resolve to an operation.
   - **`producingService`** names the *immediate* producer the screen calls — normally the screen's **co-located BFF route** (folded into the `agent:ui` issue per GUID-GOV-PROC-015), which consumes the backend API named in the shared contract.
   - **`dependencyTier` and done-ness.** T2 (default) means the UI/BFF can be built against the contract/stub before the producer merges — it controls *dispatch ordering*, not done-ness. **A T2 binding is DONE only when its producer is built, served, and passes contract verification against `contractRef`;** a permanent stub is a failure (enforced by the arch-health-check runtime-cohesion gate). Use T1 only when live data is needed to build/verify the screen.

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#the-app-foundation-contract-kind-foundation]

### The app-foundation contract (`kind: "foundation"`)

The screens of one Presentation application are **not** independent — they share an application foundation: the framework shell, route/navigation scaffold, global providers (server-state client, theme), the design-token → CSS pipeline, and the BFF client. That shared foundation is a real prerequisite that the per-screen `dataBindings` cannot express (those only point at *backend* services). Left implicit, every screen issue appears independently dispatchable and N agents each re-scaffold — and collide on — the same application from a cold start.

The UI Contract makes it explicit through two fields:

- **`kind`** — `"screen"` (default) or `"foundation"`. Exactly **one `kind: "foundation"` contract per Presentation component (app)** declares its shared shell. Its `screens[]` describes the app shell itself (route `/`, layout landmarks, skip-link, top-level error boundary, the shell's own loading/empty/error states); its `constraints[]` carry the app-wide `TS-UI-*` rules established once per app (layout, component library, global state, navigation, CI/test pipeline).
- **`dependsOn`** — UI Contract IDs this contract requires. **Every `kind: "screen"` contract MUST list its app's foundation contract in `dependsOn`.** This is the intra-frontend edge; `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` emits it as a `Prerequisite (T1)` so the foundation issue is built before any screen, and `/eap-decom-spec-plan-sequence` reports the app as **foundation (1) → screens (parallel) → tests**. Reserve the `-000` sequence (e.g. `UIC-DSH-000`) for an app's foundation contract so it sorts first.

This is the Presentation-layer instance of the general **foundation-before-fan-out** rule (GUID-GOV-PROC-015); the same rule applies to cloud environments, code components, and test harnesses, each declared in the logical architecture.
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#lifecycle]

### Lifecycle

`proposed` → `approved` → `implemented` → (`superseded`). A contract is authored `proposed`; after human review it is marked `approved`. **The pipeline must not dispatch a UI feature's implementation issue until its contract is `approved`** — this is the gate that prevents UI from being skipped. The app-foundation contract follows the same lifecycle and gate, and must be `approved` before any of its screens dispatch.
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#authoring]

### Authoring

The UI Contract is authored by the `/eap-decom-ui-contract-create` command, which:

1. Resolves the feature's `@UI` scenarios, its `Layer = Presentation` component, the `TS-UI-*` tech-specs, governing ADRs/framework, and the backend service contracts it consumes.
2. Delegates the **design thinking** to the `/ui-designer` skill (layout, states, ARIA patterns, data bindings) — the skill returns analysis; it does not write files.
3. Assembles and **validates** the JSON against the UI Contract schema, assigns the `UIC-*` id, writes it to `docs/design/ui-contracts/<concern>/`, and updates the traceability matrix.

The skill performs cognitive analysis; the command performs workflow orchestration and persistence — the same skill/command boundary the rest of the pipeline observes (STD-TEC-AI-001).
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#enterprise-standards-the-contract-grounds-in]

### Enterprise standards the contract grounds in

- `STD-APP-ACC-001` (accessibility), `STD-APP-FE-001` (frontend), `STD-APP-UI-001` (styling)
- `PTN-APP-FE-*`, `PTN-APP-MFE-*` (frontend / micro-frontend patterns)
- `GUID-APP-UI-001` (design tokens and theming)
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#the-enforcement-gate]

### The enforcement gate

`/eap-sdd-health-check` fails when a `Layer = Presentation` component lacks both a `@UI` feature and an `approved` UI Contract. It **also** fails when an app with ≥1 screen contract has no `kind: "foundation"` contract (or more than one, or a screen contract that omits the foundation from `dependsOn`) — the missing app foundation is the exact gap that makes screens look concurrently dispatchable against an empty app. This converts a silent omission (UI designed but never built, or screens that collide re-scaffolding the shell) into a hard stop, and it is retroactive — running the health check on an existing project surfaces any unbuilt Presentation surface.
page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#splitting]

### Splitting

A UI Contract is 1:1 with a feature and a screen set. When a UI feature covers multiple screens and must be split, split **by screen** (each split feature carries its own functional + UI scenarios and its own UI Contract) — never separate the UI scenarios from the functional behavior they render.
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#governance-and-compliance]

## Governance and Compliance

- **Mandatory for `@UI` features** — unlike the optional IDD, a UI Contract is required and gated.
- **Accessibility is not optional** — every contract declares a WCAG conformance target and the APG patterns its screens implement; the testing layer verifies them via the contract's `accessibility.verifiedBy` gate.
- **No invented APIs** — every `dataBinding` must `$ref` a `sync-api` Seam Contract operation (`contractRef`, a JSON-Pointer into `docs/design/seam-contracts/sync-api/<service>/openapi.json`) that exists at design time; the implementing agent consumes that operation rather than defining new endpoints, and the producer is generated from the same OpenAPI operation. A binding with only a prose `source` or a bare shape name is invalid.

[strategy/guidance/processes/architecture-pipeline/GUID-GOV-PROC-014-ui-contract-authoring-guide.md#implementing-commands-and-skills]

### Implementing Commands and Skills

- `/eap-decom-ui-contract-create` — authors and validates the UI Contract (consumes `/ui-designer` analysis)
- `/ui-designer` (skill) — tactical UI/UX design analysis and `TS-UI-*` tech-specs
- `/eap-disc-conceptual-arch-create` — sets the `UI Surface` marker
- `/eap-spec-fr-create` — adds the `@UI` tag and `@FR-*-UI-*` scenarios
- `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` — surfaces the contract and gates `agent:ui` dispatch
- `/eap-sdd-health-check` — the Presentation reconciliation gate

## Change History

| Version | Date | Author | Changes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0.0 | 2026-06-28 | EA Practice | Initial UI Contract authoring guide |
| 1.1.0 | 2026-06-29 | EA Practice | Add the **app-foundation contract** (`kind: "foundation"` + `dependsOn`) — one per Presentation app declares the shared shell/providers/routing/tokens/BFF client; every screen contract depends on it (T1), so screens fan out only after the foundation is built. Extended the health-check gate to require the foundation. Instance of the general foundation-before-fan-out rule (GUID-GOV-PROC-015) |
| 1.2.0 | 2026-07-06 | James Macurak | **Shared endpoint contract (consumer-driven-contract).** `dataBindings` now require a `contractRef` `$ref`ing a design-time shared endpoint contract (OpenAPI op + response JSON Schema under `docs/design/api-contracts/`) — the single artifact the consumer binds to and the producer is generated from and verified against; a bare shape name/inline schema is no longer valid and export halts on an unresolved `contractRef`. Clarified that a T2 binding is DONE only when its producer serves contract-conforming data (runtime-cohesion gate), and that the binding's `producingService` is the screen's co-located BFF route (folded into the `agent:ui` issue). Closes the "UI shipped against stubs whose providers were never built" gap |
| 1.2.1 | 2026-07-07 | James Macurak | Reframe the `contractRef` target as the **`sync-api` class of the generalized Seam Contract** (`docs/design/seam-contracts/sync-api/`, schema `seam-contract.schema.json`) — the UI Contract is the consumer declaration for a UI↔API seam; the Seam Contract also covers `event` and `cross-cutting` seams (GUID-GOV-PROC-015). Path updated from the interim `api-contracts/` location |
| 1.3.0 | 2026-07-07 | James Macurak | **`contractRef` now targets a native OpenAPI operation (custom wrapper retired).** The `sync-api` seam contract is authored as **OpenAPI 3.1** (one `openapi.json` per backing service), not the retired custom `seam-contract.schema.json` wrapper. `contractRef` is a JSON-Pointer into that document (`.../<service>/openapi.json#/paths/<escaped-path>/<method>`) instead of a `$ref` to a per-operation custom-JSON file. Rationale: use the standard a front-end engineer already knows (low onboarding); do not invent a format. Companion: GUID-GOV-PROC-016 v1.6, GUID-GOV-PROC-015 v1.4 |
| 1.4.0 | 2026-07-08 | James Macurak | **Governed modify front door + forward change propagation for UI Contracts.** `/eap-decom-ui-contract-modify <UIC-ID> "<intent>"` is the governed way to change a shipped UI Contract: the user supplies prose intent, `/ui-designer` proposes the edit, the command writes+validates (schema + a11y gate)+bumps the contract `version` (SemVer per TS-API-VER-02) — never a hand-edit, never the agent. A post-go-live change forward-emits a NEW superseding `agent:ui` change issue (`/eap-spec-modify` -> `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues --change`); the shipped screen issue stays closed. A raw hand-edit is flagged by `/eap-sdd-health-check --drift`. Companion: GUID-GOV-PROC-016 v1.9, GUID-GOV-PROC-015 v1.7 |
| 1.5.0 | 2026-07-10 | James Macurak | **UI Contract is born versioned (drift-marker made explicit).** The required structure now names the top-level `version` field (SemVer), authored at `1.0.0` by `/eap-decom-ui-contract-create` — not back-stamped — as the contract's drift-detection marker (the UI-Contract analogue of `info.version` for OpenAPI/AsyncAPI seams). `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` reads it into the `Built-From` stamp; `/eap-sdd-health-check --drift` compares it (by **version**, not raw byte diff — a same-version reformat is not drift) to flag a shipped screen lagging a changed contract; `--modify` bumps it. Mirrors the eap-bootstrap born-correct version-basis fix. Companion: GUID-GOV-PROC-016 v1.10, GUID-GOV-PROC-015 v1.8 |
